title: Retention Policy Expression Language (RPEL) and automated export hooks
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Design and implement a small, composable retention policy expression language (RPEL) that lets tenants define conditional retention rules for prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics. RPEL will be compiled to runtime-enforced policies with first-class hooks for automated evidence exports (bundles) when rules trigger (e.g., legal hold, e-discovery, anomalous retention extension). Goal: enable flexible per-tenant retention without requiring complex UI flow changes while providing auditable, machine-readable policy artifacts for compliance teams.
rationale: Current retention surface is static per-route or per-tenant. Customers increasingly need conditional rules (retain user messages containing PII for additional review, extend retention on legal-hold tokens, sample high-risk traffic for longer retention) and deterministic audit artifacts. RPEL abstracts these patterns into a reusable language and runtime contract, reducing bespoke engineering for each customer request.
scope: Phase 1: RPEL v1 syntax and runtime evaluator for per-route/tenant policies, export hook integration to evidence pipeline, tenant UI stub (JSON editor) and API for policy management. Phase 2: UI rule authoring, safer preview/simulation, RBAC controls, built-in templates and preflight checks.
acceptance_criteria: Define RPEL v1 grammar and spec doc with examples for common retention scenarios
Implement runtime evaluator in serving control plane that can evaluate policies with <50us median overhead per request in canary
Wire export hooks so that when a policy emits 'export' or 'extend' action, an evidence bundle is queued to the existing export pipeline
Provide API endpoints for CRUD on RPEL policies with validation and dry-run endpoint
Add logging and traceable decision IDs so every retention decision produces an audit event stored in request logs
rollout_plan: 1) Merge runtime evaluator behind feature flag. 2) Deploy to staging and run policy simulator on sampled traffic. 3) Enable on beta tenants with manual monitoring. 4) Gradually enable for more tenants and add UI templates. 5) Post-rollout 2-week audit and performance review.

tradeoffs_and_decisions: We chose a small declarative language (RPEL) over a full scripting engine to reduce risk and simplify evaluation. Trade-off: expressive limitations (no Turing-complete transforms) but gains in auditability and performance. We will not support user-defined functions in v1. Export hook semantics are append-only; immediate inline exports are avoided to preserve request latency.
metrics: Policy evaluation latency (p50/p95), export bundle queue length, number of policy-triggered exports per 100K requests, false positives from policy (measured via dry-run mismatches), customer support tickets related to retention behavior.
risks: Performance regressions in hot request paths
Complex policies that are hard to reason about leading to unexpected exports
Security review delays for export hooks and audit artifact formats
mitigations: Dry-run mode and simulator before enabling any policy in production
Enforce evaluation time budgets and fail-open fail-safe defaults
Provide reversible 'extend' operations only with tenant opt-in and audit trail
Security review required before GA; created threat-model ticket
notes: Early prototype ran as a sidecar policy evaluator and matched lab testcases. Performance microbenchmarks show median eval 12us, p95 48us on control plane instances. We need an optimized C++ evaluator in the runtime for tighter latency SLOs.
